title: The surprising habits of original thinkers
speaker: Adam Grant

sentences.en: Seven years ago, a student came to me and asked me to invest in his company.
sentences.zh: 七年前,一个学生来找我 问我投资在他的公司。

sentences.en: He said, "I'm working with three friends, and we're going to try to disrupt an industry by selling stuff online."
sentences.zh: 他说,“我和三个朋友一起工作, 我们要试图通过网上销售来破坏一个行业。”

sentences.en: And I said, "OK, you guys spent the whole summer on this, right?"
sentences.zh: 我说,"好吧,你们花了整个夏天 在这一点上,对不对?"

sentences.en: "No, we all took internships just in case it doesn't work out."
sentences.zh: "不,我们都接受了实习 以防万一它不工作。"

sentences.en: "All right, but you're going to go in full time once you graduate."
sentences.zh: "好吧,但你毕业后要全时进去"

sentences.en: "Not exactly. We've all lined up backup jobs."
sentences.zh: "不尽然,我们都安排了后备任务"

sentences.en: Six months go by, it's the day before the company launches, and there is still not a functioning website.
sentences.zh: 6个月过去了, 这是公司启动的前一天, 仍然没有一个运行中的网站。

sentences.en: "You guys realize, the entire company is a website.
sentences.zh: "你们知道,整个公司是一个网站。

sentences.en: That's literally all it is." So I obviously declined to invest.
sentences.zh: 所以显然我拒绝投资

sentences.en: And they ended up naming the company Warby Parker.
sentences.zh: 最后他们给Warby Parker公司取了名字

sentences.en: (Laughter) They sell glasses online. They were recently recognized as the world's most innovative company and valued at over a billion dollars.
sentences.zh: 最近他们被公认为世界上最有创意的公司 价值超过10亿美元

sentences.en: And now? My wife handles our investments.
sentences.zh: 现在呢 我妻子负责我们的投资

sentences.en: Why was I so wrong? To find out, I've been studying people that I come to call "originals."
sentences.zh: 为什么我错得那么厉害?

sentences.en: Originals are nonconformists, people who not only have new ideas but take action to champion them.
sentences.zh: 原创者是不符合同的人,他们不仅有新想法,而且采取行动支持他们。

sentences.en: They are people who stand out and speak up.
sentences.zh: 他们是站出来大声说话的人。

sentences.en: Originals drive creativity and change in the world.
sentences.zh: 原始人推动世界的创造力和变化。

sentences.en: They're the people you want to bet on. And they look nothing like I expected.
sentences.zh: 他们是你想赌的人 跟我预想的一模一样

sentences.en: I want to show you today three things I've learned about recognizing originals and becoming a little bit more like them.
sentences.zh: 今天我想给你们展示三件事 我学到了认识原创 并变得更像它们

sentences.en: So the first reason that I passed on Warby Parker was they were really slow getting off the ground.
sentences.zh: 所以,我通过Warby Parker的第一个原因是 他们从地上下来非常缓慢。

sentences.en: Now, you are all intimately familiar with the mind of a procrastinator.
sentences.zh: 现在,你们都非常熟悉一个拖延者的思想。

sentences.en: Well, I have a confession for you. I'm the opposite. I'm a precrastinator.
sentences.zh: 我向你坦白了,我正好相反,我是个先锋

sentences.en: Yes, that's an actual term. You know that panic you feel a few hours before a big deadline when you haven't done anything yet.
sentences.zh: 是的,这是一个真正的术语。你知道,你感到恐慌 几个小时前,一个大的最后期限,你还没有做任何事情。

sentences.en: I just feel that a few months ahead of time.
sentences.zh: 我只是觉得 几个月前。

sentences.en: (Laughter) So this started early: when I was a kid, I took Nintendo games very seriously.
sentences.zh: (笑声) 所以这个开始很早: 当我还是个孩子的时候, 我非常认真地对待任天堂游戏。

sentences.en: I would wake up at 5am, start playing and not stop until I had mastered them.
sentences.zh: 我早上五点醒来 开始玩耍 直到我掌握了他们

sentences.en: Eventually it got so out of hand that a local newspaper came and did a story on the dark side of Nintendo, starring me.
sentences.zh: 最终,它变得如此失控 当地报纸来了 做一个故事 在黑暗面任天堂, 以我为主。

sentences.en: (Laughter) (Applause) Since then, I have traded hair for teeth.
sentences.zh: (笑) (掌声) 从那以后,我用头发换牙齿。

sentences.en: (Laughter) But this served me well in college, because I finished my senior thesis four months before the deadline.
sentences.zh: 但是这在大学里对我很好 因为我提前四个月完成了我的高级论文

sentences.en: And I was proud of that, until a few years ago.
sentences.zh: 我为此感到骄傲,直到几年前。

sentences.en: I had a student named Jihae, who came to me and said, "I have my most creative ideas when I'm procrastinating."
sentences.zh: 我有一个学生叫杰海, 他来找我说, "我有我最有创意的想法 当我拖延。"

sentences.en: And I was like, "That's cute, where are the four papers you owe me?"
sentences.zh: 我当时说:"好可爱啊,你欠我的四份文件呢?"

sentences.en: (Laughter) No, she was one of our most creative students, and as an organizational psychologist, this is the kind of idea that I test.
sentences.zh: 不,她是我们最有创意的学生之一 作为组织心理学家,这是我测试的一种想法。

sentences.en: So I challenged her to get some data. She goes into a bunch of companies.
sentences.zh: 所以我要她拿一些数据 她进入了一大帮公司

sentences.en: She has people fill out surveys about how often they procrastinate.
sentences.zh: 她有人们填写 调查他们多 拖延。

sentences.en: Then she gets their bosses to rate how creative and innovative they are.
sentences.zh: 然后,她让他们的老板 评分他们是多么的创造性和创新性。

sentences.en: And sure enough, the precrastinators like me, who rush in and do everything early are rated as less creative than people who procrastinate moderately.
sentences.zh: 当然,像我这样的先发制人 提前赶来 做所有事情的人 被评为 不像那些迟缓的人那么有创意

sentences.en: So I want to know what happens to the chronic procrastinators.
sentences.zh: 我想知道慢性拖延者会怎样

sentences.en: She was like, "I don't know. They didn't fill out my survey."
sentences.zh: 她说:"我不知道,他们没填我的问卷"

sentences.en: (Laughter) No, here are our results. You actually do see that the people who wait until the last minute are so busy goofing off that they don't have any new ideas.
sentences.zh: 不,这是我们的结果。你确实看到,那些等到最后一分钟的人 忙着玩忽职守,以致于他们没有任何新想法。

sentences.en: And on the flip side, the people who race in are in such a frenzy of anxiety that they don't have original thoughts either.
sentences.zh: 在反面,那些在赛场上的人 都非常的焦虑 以至于他们也没有原创的想法

sentences.en: There's a sweet spot where originals seem to live.
sentences.zh: 有一个甜蜜的地方 原创人似乎住的地方。

sentences.en: Why is this? Maybe original people just have bad work habits.
sentences.zh: 也许原创人只是工作习惯不好

sentences.en: Maybe procrastinating does not cause creativity.
sentences.zh: 也许拖延不会造成创造性。

sentences.en: To find out, we designed some experiments.
sentences.zh: 为了查出来 我们设计了一些实验

sentences.en: We asked people to generate new business ideas, and then we get independent readers to evaluate how creative and useful they are.
sentences.zh: 我们要求人们创造新的商业想法, 然后我们让独立读者来评价它们是多么的创造性和有用。

sentences.en: And some of them are asked to do the task right away.
sentences.zh: 他们中的一些人被要求马上完成这项任务。

sentences.en: Others we randomly assign to procrastinate by dangling Minesweeper in front of them for either five or 10 minutes.
sentences.zh: 其他的则是我们随机安排的 延缓的,通过在他们面前 摇晃的扫雷器 5到10分钟。

sentences.en: And sure enough, the moderate procrastinators are 16 percent more creative than the other two groups.
sentences.zh: 当然 温和的拖延者 比其他两个群体 更有16%的创造力

sentences.en: Now, Minesweeper is awesome, but it's not the driver of the effect, because if you play the game first before you learn about the task, there's no creativity boost.
sentences.zh: 现在,扫雷者是真棒, 但它不是影响驱动器, 因为如果你先玩游戏 在你了解任务之前, 没有创造力的推动。

sentences.en: It's only when you're told that you're going to be working on this problem, and then you start procrastinating, but the task is still active in the back of your mind, that you start to incubate.
sentences.zh: 只有当你被告知 你将要研究这个问题, 然后你开始拖延, 但任务仍然 活跃在你的脑海里, 你开始孵化。

sentences.en: Procrastination gives you time to consider divergent ideas, to think in nonlinear ways, to make unexpected leaps.
sentences.zh: 拖延给了你时间来考虑不同的想法, 以非线性的方式思考, 做出意想不到的飞跃。

sentences.en: So just as we were finishing these experiments, I was starting to write a book about originals, and I thought, "This is the perfect time to teach myself to procrastinate, while writing a chapter on procrastination."
sentences.zh: 就在我们完成这些实验的时候, 我开始写一本关于原创的书, 我想,“现在正是教自己拖延的好时机, 同时写关于拖延的一章。”

sentences.en: So I metaprocrastinated, and like any self-respecting precrastinator, I woke up early the next morning and I made a to-do list with steps on how to procrastinate.
sentences.zh: 于是我超越了程序, 就像任何自尊心的先发制人一样, 第二天早上我醒来, 我做了一个待办清单, 上面写了如何拖延的步骤。

sentences.en: (Laughter) And then I worked diligently toward my goal of not making progress toward my goal.
sentences.zh: 然后,我辛勤地工作 争取我的目标 即不取得进展 我的目标。

sentences.en: I started writing the procrastination chapter, and one day -- I was halfway through -- I literally put it away in mid-sentence for months.
sentences.zh: 我开始写延缓的一章, 有一天,我半途而废, 我实际上把它放在半句中数月。

sentences.en: It was agony. But when I came back to it, I had all sorts of new ideas.
sentences.zh: 很痛苦,但当我回到那里时, 我有很多新的想法。

sentences.en: As Aaron Sorkin put it, "You call it procrastinating. I call it thinking."
sentences.zh: 正如亚伦·索金所说,“你称之为拖延,我称之为思考。”

sentences.en: And along the way I discovered that a lot of great originals in history were procrastinators.
sentences.zh: 一直以来,我发现 历史上很多伟大的原创都是拖延的。

sentences.en: Take Leonardo da Vinci. He toiled on and off for 16 years on the Mona Lisa.
sentences.zh: 带Leonardo da Vinci去,他在蒙娜丽莎上工作了16年

sentences.en: He felt like a failure. He wrote as much in his journal.
sentences.zh: 他觉得自己是个失败者 他在日记上也写了那么多

sentences.en: But some of the diversions he took in optics transformed the way that he modeled light and made him into a much better painter.
sentences.zh: 但一些他以光学方式 转移注意力的方式 改变了他模拟光线的方式 使他变成了一个更好的画家

sentences.en: What about Martin Luther King, Jr.? The night before the biggest speech of his life, the March on Washington, he was up past 3am, rewriting it.
sentences.zh: 小马丁路德金呢?

sentences.en: He's sitting in the audience waiting for his turn to go onstage, and he is still scribbling notes and crossing out lines.
sentences.zh: 他坐在观众中 等着轮到他上台 他还在写笔记 越线

sentences.en: When he gets onstage, 11 minutes in, he leaves his prepared remarks to utter four words that changed the course of history: "I have a dream."
sentences.zh: 当他上台时,11分钟内, 他把准备好的演讲 留给了四个词, 改变了历史的走向: "我有一个梦想。"

sentences.en: That was not in the script. By delaying the task of finalizing the speech until the very last minute, he left himself open to the widest range of possible ideas.
sentences.zh: 剧本上没有写到这一点,他把演讲的定稿工作推迟到最后一分钟,从而让自己对各种可能的想法持开放态度。

sentences.en: And because the text wasn't set in stone, he had freedom to improvise.
sentences.zh: 并且因为文字没有刻在石头上, 他有即兴创作的自由。

sentences.en: Procrastinating is a vice when it comes to productivity, but it can be a virtue for creativity.
sentences.zh: 在生产力方面,拖延是一种弊端,但它可以是创造力的美德。

sentences.en: What you see with a lot of great originals is that they are quick to start but they're slow to finish.
sentences.zh: 你所看到的很多伟大的原创 是他们很快开始 但他们缓慢完成。

sentences.en: And this is what I missed with Warby Parker.
sentences.zh: 这就是我对Warby Parker的怀念

sentences.en: When they were dragging their heels for six months, I looked at them and said, "You know, a lot of other companies are starting to sell glasses online."
sentences.zh: 当他们拖着脚跟6个月, 我看着他们说, “你知道,很多其他公司 开始在网上卖眼镜。”

sentences.en: They missed the first-mover advantage. But what I didn't realize was they were spending all that time trying to figure out how to get people to be comfortable ordering glasses online.
sentences.zh: 他们错过了第一个机会的优势。但我没想到的是,他们一直在想 如何让人们在网上买杯子。

sentences.en: And it turns out the first-mover advantage is mostly a myth.
sentences.zh: 结果发现第一波优势 大部分是神话

sentences.en: Look at a classic study of over 50 product categories, comparing the first movers who created the market with the improvers who introduced something different and better.
sentences.zh: 看看对50多个产品类别的典型研究,将创造市场的第一批推动者与引进不同和更好的产品的改进者进行比较。

sentences.en: What you see is that the first movers had a failure rate of 47 percent, compared with only 8 percent for the improvers.
sentences.zh: 你看到的是,第一批搬运工的故障率为47%,而改良工的故障率为8%。

sentences.en: Look at Facebook, waiting to build a social network until after Myspace and Friendster.
sentences.zh: 看看脸书 等着建立社交网络 直到Myspace和Friendter之后

sentences.en: Look at Google, waiting for years after Altavista and Yahoo.
sentences.zh: 看看Google 等待阿尔塔维斯塔和雅虎多年

sentences.en: It's much easier to improve on somebody else's idea than it is to create something new from scratch.
sentences.zh: 比起从零开始创造新东西 更容易改进别人的想法

sentences.en: So the lesson I learned is that to be original you don't have to be first.
sentences.zh: 所以,我学到的教训是,要成为原创 你不必是第一。

sentences.en: You just have to be different and better.
sentences.zh: 你只要变的更好就好

sentences.en: But that wasn't the only reason I passed on Warby Parker.
sentences.zh: 但那不是我通过Warby Parker的唯一原因

sentences.en: They were also full of doubts. They had backup plans lined up, and that made me doubt that they had the courage to be original, because I expected that originals would look something like this.
sentences.zh: 他们也充满了疑虑。他们有备用计划,这让我怀疑他们是否有勇气成为原创者,因为我期望原创会像这样。

sentences.en: (Laughter) Now, on the surface, a lot of original people look confident, but behind the scenes, they feel the same fear and doubt that the rest of us do.
sentences.zh: 现在,在表面上,很多 原始人看起来有信心, 但在幕后,他们感到同样的恐惧 和怀疑,我们其他人做的。

sentences.en: They just manage it differently. Let me show you: this is a depiction of how the creative process works for most of us.
sentences.zh: 他们只是用不同的方式管理它。让我向大家展示一下:这是关于创造性过程如何对我们大多数人起作用的描述。

sentences.en: (Laughter) Now, in my research, I discovered there are two different kinds of doubt.
sentences.zh: 现在,在我的研究中, 我发现有两种不同的怀疑。

sentences.en: There's self-doubt and idea doubt. Self-doubt is paralyzing.
sentences.zh: 自我怀疑和想法怀疑 自我怀疑正在瘫痪

sentences.en: It leads you to freeze. But idea doubt is energizing.
sentences.zh: 它让你冻僵了 但想法的怀疑是振奋人心的

sentences.en: It motivates you to test, to experiment, to refine, just like MLK did.
sentences.zh: 它激励你测试 实验 精炼 就像MLK一样

sentences.en: And so the key to being original is just a simple thing of avoiding the leap from step three to step four.
sentences.zh: 因此,成为原创的关键 仅仅是一个简单的事情 避免跳跃 从第三步到第四步。

sentences.en: Instead of saying, "I'm crap," you say, "The first few drafts are always crap, and I'm just not there yet."
sentences.zh: 而不是说,"我是垃圾," 你说,"前几个草稿 总是垃圾, 而我只是还没有。"

sentences.en: So how do you get there? Well, there's a clue, it turns out, in the Internet browser that you use.
sentences.zh: 你是怎么到那里去的?

sentences.en: We can predict your job performance and your commitment just by knowing what web browser you use.
sentences.zh: 我们可以预测你的工作表现 和你的奉献 只要知道你使用什么网络浏览器。

sentences.en: Now, some of you are not going to like the results of this study -- (Laughter) But there is good evidence that Firefox and Chrome users significantly outperform Internet Explorer and Safari users.
sentences.zh: 现在,你们中有些人不会喜欢这个研究的结果-- (笑声) 但是有很好的证据证明 Firefox 和 Chrome 的用户大大超过 Internet Explorer和Safari 的用户。

sentences.en: Yes. (Applause) They also stay in their jobs 15 percent longer, by the way.
sentences.zh: 是的。 (掌声) 他们也留在自己的工作 15%更长,顺便说一句。

sentences.en: Why? It's not a technical advantage. The four browser groups on average have similar typing speed and they also have similar levels of computer knowledge.
sentences.zh: 为什么?这不是一个技术优势。平均而言,四个浏览器组的打字速度相似,而且计算机知识水平也相似。

sentences.en: It's about how you got the browser. Because if you use Internet Explorer or Safari, those came preinstalled on your computer, and you accepted the default option that was handed to you.
sentences.zh: 这是关于你是如何得到浏览器的。因为如果你使用 Internet Explorer 或 Safari, 这些是预先安装在你的电脑上, 你接受了交给你的默认选项 。

sentences.en: If you wanted Firefox or Chrome, you had to doubt the default and ask, is there a different option out there, and then be a little resourceful and download a new browser.
sentences.zh: 如果您想要Firefox或Chrome, 您必须怀疑默认值, 并询问, 是否有不同的选项, 然后是一个有点机智 并下载一个新的浏览器 。

sentences.en: So people hear about this study and they're like, "Great, if I want to get better at my job, I just need to upgrade my browser?"
sentences.zh: 所以人们听说这个研究,他们喜欢, “很好,如果我想 得到更好的我的工作,我只需要提升我的浏览器?"

sentences.en: (Laughter) No, it's about being the kind of person who takes the initiative to doubt the default and look for a better option.
sentences.zh: 不,这是关于 那种人 谁采取主动 怀疑违约 并寻找更好的选择。

sentences.en: And if you do that well, you will open yourself up to the opposite of déjà vu.
sentences.zh: 如果你做得那么好,你就会向似曾相识的对面敞开心扉。

sentences.en: There's a name for it. It's called vuja de.
sentences.zh: 有个名字叫"华雅德"

sentences.en: (Laughter) Vuja de is when you look at something you've seen many times before and all of a sudden see it with fresh eyes.
sentences.zh: (笑声) Vuja de是当你看到的东西 你以前见过很多次 突然看到它 以新鲜的眼睛。

sentences.en: It's a screenwriter who looks at a movie script that can't get the green light for more than half a century.
sentences.zh: 是个编剧 看的电影剧本 半个多世纪都买不到绿灯

sentences.en: In every past version, the main character has been an evil queen.
sentences.zh: 在过去的每个版本里 主角都是邪恶的女王

sentences.en: But Jennifer Lee starts to question whether that makes sense.
sentences.zh: 但珍妮弗李开始质疑 这是否合理。

sentences.en: She rewrites the first act, reinvents the villain as a tortured hero and Frozen becomes the most successful animated movie ever.
sentences.zh: 她改写了第一部戏 重塑了恶棍 成为受折磨的英雄 冷冻成了有史以来最成功的动画片

sentences.en: So there's a simple message from this story.
sentences.zh: 故事中有一个简单的信息。

sentences.en: When you feel doubt, don't let it go. (Laughter) What about fear?
sentences.zh: 当你感到怀疑,不要让它去。 (笑声)什么恐惧?

sentences.en: Originals feel fear, too. They're afraid of failing, but what sets them apart from the rest of us is that they're even more afraid of failing to try.
sentences.zh: 原始人也有恐惧感,他们害怕失败 但他们和我们其他人不同之处在于 他们更害怕失败

sentences.en: They know you can fail by starting a business that goes bankrupt or by failing to start a business at all.
sentences.zh: 他们知道你可以失败 开办一个破产的企业 或完全没有开办一个企业。

sentences.en: They know that in the long run, our biggest regrets are not our actions but our inactions.
sentences.zh: 他们知道,从长远来看,我们最大的遗憾不是我们的行动,而是我们的无所作为。

sentences.en: The things we wish we could redo, if you look at the science, are the chances not taken.
sentences.zh: 我们想重做的东西, 如果你看看科学, 是没有机会。

sentences.en: Elon Musk told me recently, he didn't expect Tesla to succeed.
sentences.zh: 伊隆·穆斯克最近告诉我 他没想到特斯拉会成功

sentences.en: He was sure the first few SpaceX launches would fail to make it to orbit, let alone get back, but it was too important not to try.
sentences.zh: 他确信,最初几枚SpaceX卫星的发射将无法进入轨道,更不用说返回轨道了,但这太重要了,不能尝试。

sentences.en: And for so many of us, when we have an important idea, we don't bother to try.
sentences.zh: 对我们这么多人来说, 当我们有一个重要的想法, 我们不费吹灰之力。

sentences.en: But I have some good news for you. You are not going to get judged on your bad ideas.
sentences.zh: 但我有些好消息要告诉你 你不会因为你的坏主意而受到评判的

sentences.en: A lot of people think they will. If you look across industries and ask people about their biggest idea, their most important suggestion, 85 percent of them stayed silent instead of speaking up.
sentences.zh: 很多人认为他们可以。如果你跨行业去问人们他们最大的想法,他们最重要的建议,85%的人保持沉默,而不是说话。

sentences.en: They were afraid of embarrassing themselves, of looking stupid.
sentences.zh: 他们害怕自己丢脸 害怕看起来愚蠢

sentences.en: But guess what? Originals have lots and lots of bad ideas, tons of them, in fact.
sentences.zh: 但你知道吗 原创人有很多坏主意

sentences.en: Take the guy who invented this. Do you care that he came up with a talking doll so creepy that it scared not only kids but adults, too?
sentences.zh: 你介意他想出一个会说话的娃娃吗?

sentences.en: No. You celebrate Thomas Edison for pioneering the light bulb.
sentences.zh: 号你庆祝托马斯爱迪生 开创灯泡。

sentences.en: (Laughter) If you look across fields, the greatest originals are the ones who fail the most, because they're the ones who try the most.
sentences.zh: (笑声) 如果你跨过田野, 最伟大的原创是那些最失败的人, 因为他们是最努力的人。

sentences.en: Take classical composers, the best of the best.
sentences.zh: 带上古典作曲家 最好的

sentences.en: Why do some of them get more pages in encyclopedias than others and also have their compositions rerecorded more times?
sentences.zh: 为什么有些人在百科全书中得到的页面比其他人多,而且他们的作品重录的次数也更多?

sentences.en: One of the best predictors is the sheer volume of compositions that they generate.
sentences.zh: 最好的预测因素之一是它们所产生成份的庞大数量。

sentences.en: The more output you churn out, the more variety you get and the better your chances of stumbling on something truly original.
sentences.zh: 产出越多,你得到的种类越多 就越有机会在真正原创的东西上绊倒

sentences.en: Even the three icons of classical music -- Bach, Beethoven, Mozart -- had to generate hundreds and hundreds of compositions to come up with a much smaller number of masterpieces.
sentences.zh: 即使是古典音乐的三个图标 -- -- 巴赫、贝多芬、莫扎特 -- -- 也必须制作成数百种作品,才能产生出数量少得多的杰作。

sentences.en: Now, you may be wondering, how did this guy become great without doing a whole lot?
sentences.zh: 现在,你可能想知道, 如何这家伙变得伟大 没有做很多事?

sentences.en: I don't know how Wagner pulled that off.
sentences.zh: 我不知道瓦格纳是怎么做到的

sentences.en: But for most of us, if we want to be more original, we have to generate more ideas.
sentences.zh: 但是,对于我们大多数人来说,如果我们要更富有创意,我们就必须提出更多想法。

sentences.en: The Warby Parker founders, when they were trying to name their company, they needed something sophisticated, unique, with no negative associations to build a retail brand, and they tested over 2,000 possibilities before they finally put together
sentences.zh: Warby Parker的创始人, 当他们试图给公司命名时, 他们需要一些尖端的,独特的, 没有负面的协会 来建立一个零售品牌,

sentences.en: Warby and Parker. So if you put all this together, what you see is that originals are not that different from the rest of us.
sentences.zh: Warby和Parker 所以如果你把这些都拼凑在一起 你看到的是原创和我们没有那么不同

sentences.en: They feel fear and doubt. They procrastinate.
sentences.zh: 他们感到恐惧和怀疑,他们拖延。

sentences.en: They have bad ideas. And sometimes, it's not in spite of those qualities but because of them that they succeed.
sentences.zh: 他们有坏主意,有时,他们成功不是不顾这些品质,而是因为他们。

sentences.en: So when you see those things, don't make the same mistake I did.
sentences.zh: 所以当你看到那些东西时 不要犯和我一样的错误

sentences.en: Don't write them off. And when that's you, don't count yourself out either.
sentences.zh: 别把它们写下来 当是你的时候 也别把自己算进去

sentences.en: Know that being quick to start but slow to finish can boost your creativity, that you can motivate yourself by doubting your ideas and embracing the fear of failing to try, and that you need a lot of bad ideas in order to get a few good ones.
sentences.zh: 知道快速开始但完成速度缓慢可以提高你的创造力, 你可以通过怀疑你的想法来激励自己, 接受对失败的恐惧, 并且你需要很多坏想法来获得一些好想法。

sentences.en: Look, being original is not easy, but I have no doubt about this: it's the best way to improve the world around us.
sentences.zh: 听着,成为原始人并不容易, 但我对此毫不怀疑:这是改善我们周围世界的最好办法。

sentences.en: Thank you. (Applause)
sentences.zh: 谢谢。 （掌声）
